## Architecture §3.2 (verbatim)
- ExplorerClient.lookup(fen, { ratings, speeds }) returns { moves: { san, games, white, draws, black }[], totalGames }.
- Responses are cached in SQLite by (fen, ratings, speeds) for 30 days, since opening statistics barely change. The client sends one request at a time and treats an unreachable explorer as "out of book."
- Authentication: anonymous requests return a 401, so the client sends Authorization: Bearer ${LICHESS_TOKEN}.
- Error mapping: a 401 throws a configuration error with a clear message. A 429 honors Retry-After and that lookup is treated as out of book. A 5xx or a network error is also treated as out of book, so the game continues.
- Contract: Lichess's JSON is parsed with a zod schema into our own ExplorerResult type. A change on their side breaks only this package.

## Spike 002 (measured against the live API, 2026-11-07)
- GET https://explorer.lichess.ovh/lichess?... anonymous -> 401. With Authorization: Bearer <personal token, no permissions> -> 200, 0.36–0.45 s each.
- Success headers: cache-control: max-age=86400; no X-RateLimit-* or Retry-After on success. Rate limits undocumented, so be conservative: one request at a time; on 429 wait Retry-After seconds if present, else 60 s, before the next network request; lookups during that cooldown return out of book without fetching.
- Query used: play=d2d4,g8f6,c1f4&speeds=blitz,rapid&ratings=1200,1400&moves=6&topGames=0&recentGames=0. Use the fen= parameter instead of play= (our callers have a FEN), keep topGames=0&recentGames=0, and make moves= configurable (default 12).
- Response as received (verbatim; record it as a fixture in test/fixtures/, extending moves with the rows below):
```json

Parse leniently for unknown extra fields (zod object, not strict).

## Our types (coordinator's design; you may add fields, report changes in contract_gaps)
```ts
interface ExplorerMove { uci: string; san: string; games: number; white: number; draws: number; black: number; averageRating: number }
type OutOfBookReason = "rate_limited" | "server_error" | "network" | "timeout" | "bad_response";
interface ExplorerResult {
  moves: ExplorerMove[];       // sorted by games, descending
  totalGames: number;          // white + draws + black of the position
  opening: { eco: string; name: string } | null;
  unavailable?: OutOfBookReason; // set only when Lichess couldn't answer; then moves [] and totalGames 0
}
interface LookupOptions { ratings: number[]; speeds: string[] }  // from config: ratings [1200, 1400], speeds ["blitz", "rapid"]
class ExplorerConfigError extends Error {}  // 401, or a missing/empty token at construction
createExplorerClient(opts: { token: string; cache: ExplorerCache; fetch?: typeof fetch; now?: () => number; timeoutMs?: number /* default 3000 */; baseUrl?: string; moves?: number }): { lookup(fen: string, o: LookupOptions): Promise<ExplorerResult> }
interface ExplorerCache { get(key: string, nowMs: number): ExplorerResult | undefined; set(key: string, value: ExplorerResult, nowMs: number): void }
createSqliteExplorerCache(path: string /* ":memory:" in tests */, ttlMs?: number /* default 30 days */): ExplorerCache & { close(): void }
```
- Cache key: normalised fen + sorted ratings + sorted speeds (order of options must not matter). Table explorer_cache (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, body TEXT NOT NULL, fetched_at INTEGER NOT NULL). Expired entries are refetched and overwritten.
- Never cache an unavailable result.
- One request at a time: concurrent lookup calls are serialised (a queue), and two concurrent lookups of the same key make one network request.
- The token is a constructor argument; reading process.env.LICHESS_TOKEN belongs to the server, not this package. Never log or include the token in an error message.
